title: Our Story — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: The Director's message, the founding story, the crest, the CLEVER Standard, who answers for each of the five institutions, what happens when something goes wrong, the thirteen rooms on the campus, and the questions families ask most.
body: Our Founding and Our Standard Faith and Scholarship, One Inheritance. A hybrid Islamic and secular institution in Ikorodu, Lagos State — built on the conviction that a child raised well in both faith and knowledge will want for neither, and named in honour of a father who believed exactly that. Read Our Story → Meet the Founder Founded July 2016 · Ikorodu, Lagos State Five institutions · one Board of Governors Two national curricula - Nigerian and Saudi Arabian BECE · WAEC · NECO - the same papers as every other candidate in Nigeria Ijāzah examined by named scholars, entered in the register under a unique reference Gold at the SPELL Africa International Spelling Leaders Competition Independently reported by Punch Newspapers , August 2023 Thirteen dedicated rooms · three science laboratories Every document we issue is verifiable - no account, no fee Open to Muslims and non-Muslims , to sons and daughters alike A Word From Our Founder The Conviction Behind the School Founder & Director Dr. Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi B.Sc. Applied Accounting (Oxford Brookes University) · M.Sc. Financial Management (Edinburgh Business School, Heriot-Watt University) · FCCA (UK) · FCA (ICAN) · Doctoral Candidate, Edgewood University, Madison, Wisconsin Governance is what keeps a good intention alive after the person who had it has gone. On why the Board can overrule him It is my privilege to welcome you to Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools, a hybrid Islamic and secular institution built in Ikorodu, Lagos State, on a single conviction: that faith and scholarship are one inheritance, not two, and that a child raised well in both will want for neither. As Director, I hold our staff and our institution to that standard in a school that is secure, orderly and genuinely inclusive. My father, Anofi Aliu Akano, was a clerk at the Nigerian Ports Authority. He did not live to see this school. It was built after he died, in the year my younger brother and I were serving the country under the NYSC, which is to say it was built by two young men with very little, out of an obligation neither of us had to discuss with the other. The two decades I then spent in banking, insurance, oil and gas, and consulting taught me the unglamorous half of building an institution. Governance is what keeps a good intention alive after the person who had it has gone. An organisation without accounts, minutes and published policy has good intentions and nothing else. That is the discipline I have tried to put underneath this school: a Board of Governors that can overrule me, policies any parent may read in full, and a register in which every result and every certificate we issue can be checked long after all of us are gone. Our doors are open to Muslims and non-Muslims, to sons and daughters alike. Every educator here is expected to send a child out able to sit a national examination, hold a Qur'anic text in memory, argue a position honestly, and earn a living, and to be judged on whether that happens. Whether you are considering us for the first time, already a parent in our community, or returning as one of our own alumni, you are welcome here. SHRS Dr. Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi Founder, Chairman of the Board of Governors & Head of Schools Faith and scholarship are not rival inheritances. They are one and the same. body: The Academic Programme One Standard. Five Institutions. A Lifetime of Learning. From a child's first morning in Nursery to the day a student recites the whole Qur'an from memory, every Sultan Hanafi institution is held to one CLEVER standard: rigorous secular scholarship and deep Islamic formation, taught not side by side but as one. Begin an Application → Compare the Institutions Our Academic Philosophy Faith and Scholarship, Held to One Standard A child raised well in both faith and scholarship will want for neither. That single conviction is the reason Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools exists, and the reason we refused to make families choose between a strong secular education and a serious Islamic one. So we built five institutions rather than one. Each carries its own age range, curriculum and learning model: a Nursery and Primary School, a secondary Royal College, a School of Islamic and Arabic Studies, a Qur'an College, and a new Online & Distance Learning School. What they share is more important than what separates them. One Board of Governors. One CLEVER standard. One campus in Ikorodu, Lagos that welcomes Muslims and non-Muslims, sons and daughters, alike. The result is a continuous path. A family can begin with a two-year-old learning to read and to pray in the same week, and stay with us through examinations, memorisation of the Qur'an, and beyond, never once stepping outside a community that holds academic excellence and Islamic character to the same measure. 0 Institutions One Board of Governors 0 National Examinations BECE, WAEC and NECO 0 National Curricula Nigerian & Saudi Arabian 0 Learning Stages Nursery to graduation 0 Rooted in Ikorodu Imowonla community, Lagos A child raised well in both faith and scholarship will want for neither. The conviction on which this school was founded The CLEVER Standard One Standard, Held in Six Values CLEVER is the measure every teacher is held to, in all five of our institutions, from a two-year-old's first morning to the day a student is granted an Ijazah: the classical licence to teach the Qur'an, awarded only after reciting the whole of it from memory to a named scholar. Creativity Children are taught to build things. Entrepreneurship, applied technology and problem-solving are timetabled subjects from the early years upward, and Coding sits on the Junior School's own assessment schedule. Leadership Prefectships, competitions and service give students the chance to lead early — and the character formation to lead justly, as Islam asks of them. Engagement Parents are treated as partners and kept close to the life of their children. Any safety incident, any illness beyond minor first aid, and any substantive disciplinary matter reaches the guardian the same day. Versatility Two national curricula, five institutions and flexible timetables let a family shape a path that fits their child — day or boarding, weekday or weekend, on campus or online. Ethics Daily Islamic character formation is the ground everything else is built on. Honesty, worship and adab are taught explicitly, modelled by staff, and expected in a child's daily conduct. Reliability A verifiable credential system, a published calendar and a governance charter mean families can trust what the school says — and check it. The question a sceptical parent should ask is where that claim is written down and who signs it. Three places. In the published timetable. Tuesday, English & Diction, Business Studies and Social & Citizenship. Wednesday, Integrated Science, Yoruba and Digital Technology. Thursday, History and Coding. title: Boarding Facility — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: Full and half boarding for College & Qur'an memorisation students aged 9–16, in a home-like, supportive environment.
body: Student Life The Boarding Life Centre Discover a community where friendships flourish and memories are made. Our home-like boarding accommodation provides a comfortable environment in which boarders experience cordial relationships with roommates, creating a supportive and immersive learning environment. Boarders enjoy extra academic and extra-curricular support, more time to read and use a wide range of facilities, and the opportunity for self-reflection and discovery — including after-class Islamic lectures and post-Salah admonitions. Eligibility College & Qur'an memorisation students, ages 9–16 Full Boarding Monday to Sunday Half Boarding Monday to Friday Other arrangements Feasible by family schedule/budget Boarding Life The Dining Hall Boarders share meals together in a home-like dining setting, part of the daily rhythm of life on the boarding campus. A Day in Boarding Life The Daily Routine A structured schedule published to guardians, not left to vary informally — covering wake time, prayer, meals, study, memorisation, and rest. Wake & Fajr The boarding day begins before dawn, with wake time and the Fajr prayer. Morning Routine & Meals Preparation for the school day, followed by breakfast in the dining hall. Academic Day Full attendance at lessons alongside day students, with the same curriculum and teachers. Prayer Times & Meals The five daily prayers and mealtimes structure the afternoon and evening, observed together as a boarding house. Study Hours Supervised evening study, with extra academic support built into the boarding routine. Qur'an Memorisation & Muraja'ah Qur'an College boarders keep a dedicated memorisation and revision (Muraja'ah) session as part of the evening routine. Islamic Lectures & Admonitions After-class Islamic lectures and post-Salah admonitions, part of the reflective rhythm of boarding life. Free Time & Lights-Out Free time on the Recreation Ground or in the CCA Room, followed by a fixed lights-out with a logged room check. Supervision, Welfare & Safety Never Left Unsupervised From the Boarding Regulations (SD-04) Continuous Overnight Supervision Boarding supervision is continuous — there is no unsupervised overnight period, even during sleeping hours. A room check is conducted at lights-out and at least once more during the night, logged by name and time, with at least one warden awake and present in each boarding house overnight and a second reachable within the site. Safeguarding & Pastoral Care The Same Standard, Around the Clock The staff-student contact rules in the Child Protection & Safeguarding Policy apply in full to boarding staff. A new boarding student's first weeks receive additional pastoral check-ins beyond the standard routine, and any safety incident, illness beyond minor first aid, or substantive disciplinary matter is communicated to the guardian the same day. For Parents & Guardians Leave-Out & Staying Connected Leave-Out Authorisation Every Departure, Logged and Authorised A boarding student leaves the premises only with prior guardian authorisation, logged by the boarding warden. Guardians are entitled to request a call with the boarding warden within a reasonable response window — boarding is a partnership with the family, not a handover. Frequently Asked Questions Who is eligible to board? ▾ Boarding is available to Royal College and Qur'an College students aged 9 to 16. Full boarding runs Monday to Sunday; half boarding runs Monday to Friday. Other arrangements can be discussed with the school based on family schedule and budget. What's the difference between full and half boarding? ▾ Full boarding students remain on campus the whole week, including weekends. Half boarding students board Monday to Friday and return home for the weekend. Is a boarder ever left unsupervised overnight? ▾ No. Supervision is continuous, with room checks at lights-out and again during the night, and at least one warden awake in each boarding house at all times, per the Boarding Regulations

title: Digital Qur'an Centre — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: What's real today toward a daily Qur'an companion, and the legally-clean path for the full Madinah-style reader.
body: The Digital Qur'ān Centre A Daily Companion to the Book Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools was founded on the conviction that the Qur'ān is not a subject on a timetable but the discipline around which a life is ordered. The Digital Qur'ān Centre carries that conviction into the instruments a household actually uses: the adhkār of the morning and the evening, the record of a child's memorisation, and the daily portion that opens the school's own front page. In Service Today The Adhkār Centre The adhkār of the morning and the evening, each with its Arabic, its transliteration, its meaning and its citation, and each set to the number of repetitions the Sunnah prescribes. A smart tasbīḥ counter keeps the tally; recitation is read aloud; the household's own consistency is recorded in streaks and marked in attainments. Enter the Adhkār Centre . The Ḥifẓ and Ijāzah Record Every pupil enrolled in Sultan Hanafi Qur'ān College carries a formal record of memorisation: status by juz', the teacher's murāja'ah notes, and progress toward Ijāzah. That record is kept by the College and is visible to the pupil's guardian in the Parent Portal, so that a family may follow the journey without having to ask for it. See Qur'ān College and the Digital Campus . Today's Wird A daily portion — the adhkār appointed to the hour, and a well-established verse or ḥadīth with its citation — greets every visitor on the school's front page, before any word of admissions or fees. It is placed first because it is first. See Today's Wird . The Sultan Royal Annual Competition The institution's own annual competition, held for excellence in the Qur'ān, in the Arabic language, and in the adhān. It is the occasion on which the school measures publicly what it teaches privately. The Standard This Centre Holds Itself To A school that teaches the Qur'ān may not publish its text carelessly. Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools will place a complete Muṣḥaf reader in this Centre — the full six hundred and four pages, verse-by-verse recitation, and the repeat-loop instruments a ḥāfiẓ needs for murāja'ah — and it will do so only from a text of established provenance, typeset in an authentic script, and reviewed by qualified scholars before a single āyah is displayed. The standards below are the ones the institution has adopted for that work. Standard 01 · Text Provenance of the Muṣḥaf Text The Arabic text will be taken from the Tanzil Project 's Uthmānī edition — the verified text on which the established Qur'ān applications are built, released for verbatim redistribution under Creative Commons Attribution with a link to its source. No text of uncertain origin is displayed in this Centre. Standard 02 · Script Typesetting in the Madīnah Hand The reader will be set in the King Fahd Glorious Qur'ān Printing Complex's own KFGQPC Uthmānic script, which the Complex distributes for non-commercial typesetting — the authentic Madīnah letterform rather than an approximation of it. The photographic pages of the printed Madīnah Muṣḥaf stand under separate terms, and would be reproduced only upon written permission from the Complex. Standard 03 · Recitation The Voice of the Reciter Verse-by-verse recitation will be served from licensed archives, and each reciter's own terms confirmed individually before his voice is carried on this site. A reciter is a scholar, and his recitation is his work. Standard 04 · Review Scholarly Confirmation No portion of the Muṣḥaf enters this Centre until it has been read against a printed Muṣḥaf by the faculty of the School of Islamic and Arabic Studies and the Qur'ān College. Until it is, this Centre carries the instruments of daily practice and directs the reader to the printed Book and to the established Qur'ān applications for the text itself.
